--- title: "Nonlinear regression and more quantitative data visualization" subtitle: "
36-315: Statistical Graphics and Visualization, Summer 2026" footer: "[36-315-summer26.netlify.app](https://36-315-summer26.netlify.app)" format: revealjs: embed-resources: true height: 900 width: 1600 theme: theme.scss smaller: true slide-number: c/t linestretch: 1.4 code-line-numbers: false html-math-method: method: mathjax url: "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3/es5/tex-mml-chtml.js" --- ## Beyond linear regression * The truth is (almost) never linear * But often the linearity assumption is good enough * Many nonparametric/nonlinear regression methods * splines * **local regression** * generalized additive models * kernel regression * wavelets ## Nonlinear regression * Assume normality, but not linearity where $f(x)$ is some unknown function $$Y_i \stackrel{iid}{\sim} N(\underbrace{f(X_i)}, \sigma^2)$$ * Do not make explicit assumptions about the functional form of $f$ (i.e., $f$ is estimated from the data) * **Intuition: Any nonlinear function is locally linear** * Local linear regressions fits a bunch of... local linear regressions, and then glues them together * Local linear regression is basically **weighted linear regression**, where only "local units" get weight ## Weighted linear regression * In linear regression, we solve $$\arg \min_{\beta_0,\beta_1} \sum_{i=1}^n (Y_i - \beta_0 - \beta_1 X_i)^2$$ . . . * In **weighted** linear regression, we solve $$\arg \min_{\beta_0,\beta_1} \sum_{i=1}^n w_i \cdot (Y_i - \beta_0 - \beta_1 X_i)^2$$ . . . * Local linear regression is exactly the same, except the weights depend on which $x$ we want to estimate $f(x)$. ## Local linear regression via LOESS In **local linear regression**, we estimate $f(X_i)$ and solve $$\text{arg }\underset{\beta_0, \beta_1}{\text{min}} \sum_i^n w_i(x) \cdot \big(Y_i - \beta_0 - \beta_1 X_i \big)^2$$ * Notice the weights depend on $x$, so observations close to $x$ gets more weight in estimating $f(x)$ . . . `geom_smooth()` uses tri-cubic weighting: $$w_i(d_i) = \begin{cases} (1 - |d_i|^3)^3, \text{ if } i \in \text{neighborhood of } x\\ 0 \text{ if } i \notin \text{neighborhood of } x \end{cases}$$ * $d_i$: distance between $x$ and $X_i$ scaled to be between 0 and 1 * `span`: controls fraction of observations in neighborhood around the observation of interest * Default: `span = 0.75` (use 75% of the observations to fit local linear regression with weights) :::aside LOESS (Locally Estimated Scatterplot Smoothing) or LOWESS (Locally Weighted Scatterplot Smoothing) ::: ## Local linear regression, animated ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-2-1.gif){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ## Displaying trend lines: LOESS ::: columns ::: {.column} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) theme_set(theme_light()) ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggplot(aes(x = flipper_len, y = body_mass)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.5) + geom_smooth() ``` ::: * LOESS is default behavior when $n \leq 1000$ * Default `span = 0.75` * For $n > 1000$, `mgcv::gam()` is used with
`formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "cs")` and
`method = "REML"` ::: ::: {.column} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Adjusting `span` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-7-1.gif){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ## Pairs plots * Create a pairs plot to see all pairwise relationships in one plot * Pairs plot can include the various kinds of pairwise plots * Two quantitative variables: scatterplot * One categorical, one quantitative: side-by-side violins, stacked histograms, overlaid densities * Two categorical: stacked bars, side-by-side bars, mosaic plots ## Pairs plots ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(GGally) penguins |> select(bill_len, bill_dep, flipper_len, body_mass) |> ggpairs() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){fig-align='center' width=1440} ::: ::: ## Pair plots of quantitative variables ::: columns ::: {.column width="42%"} * Diagonal: marginal distributions * Off-diagonal: joint (pairwise) distributions or statistical summaries (e.g., correlation) * Matrix of plots is symmetric ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(bill_len, bill_dep, flipper_len, body_mass) |> ggpairs(aes(alpha = 0.2)) ``` ::: Syntax note: change `alpha` within `aes` (annoying...) ::: ::: {.column width="58%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Pair plots with categorical variables ::: columns ::: {.column width="43%"} * Can either use `select()` before plotting or specify `columns` directly ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggpairs(columns = c("bill_len", "body_mass", "island"), aes(alpha = 0.2, color = species)) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="57%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ::: ::: ## More customization ::: columns ::: {.column width="38%"} * Can customize which figures are displayed in which panels * For more details, check out the package documentation [here](https://ggobi.github.io/ggally/articles/ggpairs.html) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggpairs( columns = c("bill_len", "body_mass", "island"), mapping = aes(alpha = 0.2, color = species), lower = list(continuous = "smooth_lm", combo = "facetdensitystrip"), upper = list(continuous = "cor", combo = "facethist") ) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="62%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ::: ::: ## More customization ::: columns ::: {.column width="46%"} * Can also incorporate `ggplot2` customization ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggpairs(columns = c("bill_len", "bill_dep", "flipper_len"), aes(color = species, alpha = 0.2)) + scale_color_manual(values = c("orange", "blue", "cyan4")) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("orange", "blue", "cyan4")) + theme_minimal() + theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="54%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Correlation heatmaps ::: columns ::: {.column} * Use `correlate()` and `scretch()` functions from the `corrr` package to compute correlation matrix and pivot * Use `geom_tile()` to create a heatmap (tile map) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(corrr) ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(bill_len, bill_dep, flipper_len, body_mass) |> correlate(diagonal = 1) |> stretch() |> ggplot(aes(x, y, fill = r)) + geom_tile(color = "white") + scale_fill_gradient2(high = "red", mid = "white", low = "blue", midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1)) + coord_fixed() ``` ::: * See also: [`ggcorrplot`](https://rpkgs.datanovia.com/ggcorrplot) ::: ::: {.column}
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-19-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Parallel coordinates plots ::: columns ::: {.column width="42%"} * Display each variable side-by-side on standardized axis * Connect observations with lines * Useful when working with a moderate number of observations and variables
(can be overwhelming with too many) * Adjust the transparency of the lines to handle overlap ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(GGally) penguins |> select(bill_len, bill_dep, flipper_len, body_mass) |> ggparcoord(alphaLines = 0.2) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="58%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-21-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Parallel coordinates plots ::: columns ::: {.column width="45%"} * Color lines by a categorical variable * Can be useful for revealing group structure * How do we order the x-axis? ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggparcoord(columns = 3:6, alphaLines = 0.2, groupColumn = "species", order = c(6, 5, 3, 4)) + theme(legend.position = "top") ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="55%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-23-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Parallel coordinates plots ::: columns ::: {.column width="45%"} * By default, the y-axis is scaled by subtracting the mean and dividing by the standard deviation * Use `scale = "uniminmax"` so that minimum of the variable is 0 and the maximum is 1 ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> ggparcoord(columns = 3:6, alphaLines = 0.2, groupColumn = "species", scale = "uniminmax") + theme(legend.position = "top") ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="55%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture08_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-25-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ::: :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
